Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training
Minimum 5 years Business Systems Analysis Role or Equivalent

The Pension Administration BSA 3 applies broad professional knowledge of business systems analysis and UCRS administration to independently assess business needs, document requirements, and resolve system and process issues of varied scope. The position uses established analysis methods and practices to develop solutions, support system changes and testing, and improve ongoing operations. The BSA 3 collaborates with business and technical partners to help ensure systems and processes meet organizational and member service needs. Please note this is a hybrid position, three days a week on site, located in Oakland, CA.

25% Business and Systems Analysis - Applies business systems analysis knowledge to identify and define scope, objectives, and requirements for complex UCRS pension and related benefits systems and processes. Evaluates business practices, system capabilities, and end-user needs to recommend appropriate solutions.

25% Systems Specifications, Design, and Testing - Develops system and process specifications and contributes to user interface design to address business requirements. Plans and conducts unit, integration, and acceptance testing, and participates in cross-functional teams to resolve complex business and systems issues.

25% Business Process Improvement - Gathers and analyzes information to develop recommendations and documentation for business processes and procedures. Recommends and implements process improvements and works with stakeholders to clarify requirements and reach agreement on specifications.

25% Requirements, Application Support, and Guidance - Analyzes business and user needs, documents requirements, and recommends updates to system or process logic. Provides support and training for new applications and offers guidance to less-experienced Business Systems Analysts.
Business Systems Analyst 3 (TX)
This position is represented by the TX - Technical bargaining unit.
Thorough knowledge of business and process analysis functions.
Thorough Knowledge of related areas of IT.
Strong skills and knowledge of methodologies associated with analysis of processes and problems, information flow and architecture.
Demonstrated ability to work with others from diverse backgrounds.
In-depth understanding and skill in process and systems requirement documentation standards, such as Use Case modeling, User Story creations and narrative description.
Self-motivated and works independently and as part of a team. Able to learn effectively and meet deadlines. Demonstrates problem solving skills.
Demonstrated testing and test planning skills.
Broad knowledge relating to software design.

Demonstrated effective communication and interpersonal skills. Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization. Interpersonal and communications skills to work with both technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization.
Thorough knowledge of business processes and procedures.
Demonstrated knowledge and expertise in pension and benefits.
Demonstrated knowledge and expertise in identifying methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria to support and enhance the UC Retirement System.
